articles.title: 'No, not really': Marcus Trescothick unsure of future with England Test side
articles.summary: Cricket News: Marcus Trescothick is not sure if he will continue with England's Test team after Stephen Fleming takes charge as the permanent head coach.Trescothick.
articles.body: Marcus Trescothick is not sure if he will continue with England's Test team after Stephen Fleming takes charge as the permanent head coach.Trescothick was the interim head coach during England's recent 3-0 home series win over Pakistan. He took charge after Brendon McCullum left the Test coaching role, with Fleming set to take over ahead of the winter series against South Africa.Trescothick had worked as McCullum's assistant coach and is now waiting to find out whether he will remain part of the Test coaching staff under Fleming.Trescothick unsure about Test roleWhen asked if he knew what his Test role would be once Fleming takes over, Trescothick admitted that there was no clear answer yet."No, not really," Trescothick said when asked whether he had an idea of his Test role in the future, as quoted by Cricinfo. "I've spoken with Rob Key a little bit over the last couple of weeks and had bits of discussions on what might happen."I think when Stephen’s (Fleming) over and then they - Rob and Stephen and Brendon - can get together and really sort of thrash out exactly how it's going to look, then we'll probably be involved in those sort of conversations afterwards."Trescothick joins England's white-ball setupTrescothick will now travel to Southampton to join McCullum and the England white-ball team for the Sri Lanka T20I series. He will be joined by fellow assistants Sarah Taylor, Tim Southee and Jeetan Patel. Kevin Pietersen will also join the group as a specialist mentor."Our immediate plan is obviously then looking at the Sri Lanka series we're now straight into, with the possibility of going maybe into Pakistan. But I think within the next couple of weeks we'll know a bit more."I love doing both formats. It's been brilliant and (I'm) privileged to be in the position of being assistant coach where you're on the road because it's great fun and you're with the team and you're working with the best. There's nothing better than working with your own national country, of course. But we'll see. We'll see how it pans out."Joe Root praises TrescothickEngland Test captain Joe Root praised Trescothick for the way he handled the team during the Pakistan series."I think the way that he's worked with me, the way that he's worked with the group, has been outstanding," Root said. "And I hope he takes a lot of confidence from it and if he ever gets the opportunity to be a head coach further down the line, it's been great for him and he's done a brilliant job over the course of the three games."Trescothick wants England voice in Test setupTrescothick also stressed the importance of having people in the Test coaching staff who understand the specific needs of English players and the England team."As much as we can within the course of coaching systems, you want someone within that that can highlight things that are important with England players and England teams and England series that you play," said Trescothick. "Because they are different to other countries and unique in their own way."We want to try and promote our own from within and get them up to the top because there's nothing better, I don't think, than if you can get to that point. It's not the be all and end all. But, I think, as much as we can have the representation in there, then the better it'll be."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi not playing vs Afghanistan in 1st T20I?
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India made a big selection call for the first T20I against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday, with Sanju Samson ge.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India made a big selection call for the first T20I against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday, with Sanju Samson getting the nod over young batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and decided to bowl first. India also brought Jasprit Bumrah back into the playing XI and picked specialist spinner Varun Chakaravarthy ahead of Yash Thakur.Why is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi not playing?India chose experience in the opening game, with Samson selected in the XI instead of Vaibhav.Iyer also confirmed that Washington Sundar and two other players were left out, making it clear that team combination was behind the decision."It's a luxury to have him (Bumrah) in the squad -- he carries lot of great attitude when it comes to winning matches. Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, neither are Washington and two more."Iyer later explained that managing the team combination was difficult."That is more difficult, I feel, but I would say if Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, then Washington (Sundar) is not playing and there are two more which you'll get to know".Samson was named as India's wicketkeeper, with Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma also in the batting group.India also picked Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivam Dube and Axar Patel before going with Arshdeep Singh, Bumrah and Varun Chakaravarthy as the bowling options.Iyer said India had played several matches in Delhi and wanted to make use of the conditions by bowling first."We’re going to bowl first. I mean, when you have played in Delhi, you know what the pitch has got to offer and we’ve played quite a bit of matches over here. So based on that and looking at the conditions, that’s really both. [On his first ten matches as India captain]It's been a roller coaster ride, but if you see the previous series which we played against Zimbabwe, there were a lot of positives and the boys were optimistic in their approach. So, that's the attitude we've got to carry in this series as well."Jasprit Bumrah returnsBumrah returned to the India XI after missing recent assignments following the left-knee injury that ruled him out of an ODI in England and two Tests in Sri Lanka.Iyer called having Bumrah in the squad a "luxury" and highlighted his experience and ability to win matches."[On having Jasprit Bumrah available in the squad] Yes, certainly. I think it's a luxury to have him in the squad because he's immensely experienced and he carries a lot of great attitude when it comes to winning matches. So, we know he's a match winner and we know what he's got to offer."Afghanistan make changesAfghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran said his team would have bowled first had they won the toss."We would have bowled first. Unfortunately, we lost the toss and we will think about batting. We will try to put a good total on the board."Zadran said Afghanistan were excited to host India and asked fans to support both teams."Yeah, it's a great feeling for us. It is a pleasure to host India, here in India for the first time. We are trying to enjoy ourselves, trying to have a good series against them."He added: "We have got lots of support from the fans in the past as well, and just requesting them to come support, both teams. I hope they don't forget us, but hopefully they come and support their own player, their own team, and give their energy to the players."Afghanistan also made changes to their side."Naveen(-ul-Haq) is not playing, Noor Ahmad, and Abdullah (Ahmadzai) and Naveen-ul-Haq, he's not match ready for today. Yeah, we will think about him for the second and third game," Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran said.India vs Afghanistan 1st T20I: Playing XIsAfghanistan: Ibrahim Zadran (c), Rahmanullah Gurbaz (wk), Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Gulbadin Naib, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Noor Ahmad, Fazalhaq FarooqiIndia: Sanju Samson (wk), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah, Varun ChakaravarthyGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India alter winning combination for Asia Cup final vs Sri Lanka; Gunalan Kamalini replaces Pratika Rawal
articles.summary: Cricket News: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat first against Sri Lanka in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final at the Dubai International C.
articles.body: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat first against Sri Lanka in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.India have made their first change of the tournament, bringing Gunalan Kamalini into the playing XI in place of Pratika Rawal. Kamalini gets her first opportunity in this edition of the Asia Cup and will play only her second T20I for India.The change comes after India fielded an unchanged XI in their opening four matches.India aim for record eighth Asia Cup titleBoth India and Sri Lanka have remained unbeaten on their way to the final, although India have looked the more dominant side throughout the tournament. The Women in Blue have produced strong performances across batting, bowling and fielding, with Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma leading the run-scoring charts for India.With the ball, Deepti Sharma and Shree Charani have been among India's standout performers, claiming 11 and eight wickets respectively. India are chasing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title, having previously won four editions in the ODI format and three in T20Is.Sri Lanka rely on Athapaththu and DilhariSri Lanka have also reached the final unbeaten but have not been as consistent with the bat. Captain Chamari Athapaththu has managed just 63 runs from four innings, and Sri Lanka will need their top order to step up against India's strong bowling attack.Kavisha Dilhari has emerged as another key player for the defending champions and will be expected to contribute with both bat and ball in the title clash.India Women Playing XI: Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Gunalan Kamalini, Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Bharti Fulmali, Richa Ghosh (wk), Deepti Sharma, Prema Rawat, Shree Charani, Kranti Gaud, Nandani SharmaSri Lanka Women Playing XI: Chamari Athapaththu (c), Imesha Dulani, Vishmi Gunaratne, Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Kaushani Nuthyangana (wk), Sugandika Kumari, Chamudi Praboda, Mithali AyodhyaGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: After IND vs AFG first, ‘Vande Mataram’ set to become regular before India matches
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: For the first time ever, the national song, 'Vande Mataram', was sung before the match between India and Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley St.
articles.body: New Delhi: For the first time ever, the national song, 'Vande Mataram', was sung before the match between India and Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on Sunday. The national song was followed by the standard practice of national anthems of both countries.It must be mentioned here that 'Vande Mataram' was sung during the Delhi Premier League final also, which also took place at the same venue. Curiously, it was not played during other state leagues in Odisha and Punjab.It has been learnt that it is going to be a practice going forward in matches involving the Indian team in India. "This is going to be followed in all events in India going forward. It is going to be a practice and it is not just about this stadium," said a source.It comes on the heels of Parliament passing a bill that made any insult to the national song a punishable offence. The full official version of ‘Vande Mataram’ comprises six stanzas - which was sung before the first of the three match series.As the 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram' was celebrated, the Home Ministry had directed that all six stanzas must be sung when 'Jana Gana Mana' is also sung."The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amends Section 3 of the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. It extends the same legal protection to the National Song, Vande Mataram that is currently afforded to the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The amendment makes it an offence to intentionally prevent the singing of the National Song or to cause a disturbance to an assembly engaged in its singing," said a PIB statement in July.Prior to the teams taking the field for the national song and anthems, India skipper Shreyas Iyer had won the toss and chosen to field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 51 wides! Arshdeep Singh creates big unwanted record in India vs Afghanistan 1st T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Arshdeep Singh produced the standout bowling performance for India, taking 3/19 as India restricted Afghanistan to 156/8 in the opening game of the th.
articles.body: Arshdeep Singh produced the standout bowling performance for India, taking 3/19 as India restricted Afghanistan to 156/8 in the opening game of the three-match T20I series on Sunday.However, Arshdeep also bowled 51 wides, the most by any bowler for a team since January 2025.Arshdeep's 51 wides accounted for 7.4% of all the balls he bowled during the period. Renegades' R Ngarava and West Indies' Jason Holder follow with 38 wides each, while New Zealand's Jacob Duffy and West Indies' Romario Shepherd have bowled 36 each.Arshdeep strikes at crucial momentsJasprit Bumrah bowled some sharp deliveries, but Arshdeep stole the show with his 3/19 as India kept Afghanistan under pressure for most of the innings.The two spinners, Varun Chakravarthy (1/16 in 4 overs) and Axar Patel (1/27 in 4 overs), controlled the game during the first 10 overs.Bumrah (1/26 in 4 overs) also bowled at full tilt and sent down 16 dot balls. He removed former Kolkata Knight Riders batter Rahmanullah Gurbaz for a duck after the ball kicked up and Gurbaz edged it to Abhishek Sharma, who took a smart low catch at first slip.Arshdeep used variations and changes of pace to make breakthroughs at important moments.Most wides bowled since Jan 2025 (FM team)51 Arshdeep Singh (7.4% of all balls)38 R Ngarava (5.8%)/ J Holder (5.2%)36 J Duffy (5.8%)/ R Shepherd (8.6%)Arshdeep removes Nabi, Rashid strugglesIbrahim Zadran (13) and Sediqullah Atal (11) hit a few shots before a mix-up ended the Afghanistan captain's innings.Arshdeep then bowled a wide yorker that Atal tried to dig out. Bumrah, standing at fly slip, took an easy catch.Gulbadin Naib (2) played an inside-out shot against Axar Patel and was caught by Nitish Reddy. Varun then continued to attack the stumps and breached Darwish Rasooli's defence, leaving Afghanistan at 43/5 in seven overs.But Azmatullah Omarzai counter-attacked and targeted Nitish Reddy, who became the weak link in India's attack.Arshdeep returned for his second spell and clean bowled the dangerous Mohammad Nabi after being hit for a six.Once Nabi was dismissed, Afghanistan suffered another mini-collapse. Rashid Khan struggled to get going against Bumrah and Arshdeep and was eventually caught in the deep after scoring just one run from 10 balls.Omarzai keeps Afghanistan above 150Omarzai continued to fight back and smashed Shivam Dube for two sixes in the final over.The over produced 21 runs and helped Afghanistan finish on 156/8, giving the 'home' team a total of more than 150.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Abhishek Sharma’s 22-ball fifty, Arshdeep’s three-for lead India to seven-wicket win over Afghanistan in 1st T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking batting display as India began their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with a commanding seven-wicke.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking batting display as India began their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with a commanding seven-wicket victory at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.Chasing 157, India raced to 157/3 in just 13.4 overs, with Abhishek smashing 82 off only 32 balls to take the game away from Afghanistan. His innings featured seven fours and seven sixes, while Ishan Kishan provided valuable support with a composed 42.Afghanistan stumble before Omarzai-Nabi rescue actAfter being asked to bat, Afghanistan endured a dramatic collapse at the top. India's pace attack struck early, with Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and the supporting bowlers putting the visitors under pressure. Afghanistan slipped to 43/5, leaving their innings in serious danger of folding for a modest total.However, Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi launched a counterattack to revive Afghanistan's innings. The pair added 83 runs, taking the visitors past 150 and giving their bowlers something to defend.Omarzai finished unbeaten on 64 off 44 balls, while Nabi contributed 33 as Afghanistan eventually posted 156/8.India's bowlers had Afghanistan in trouble for much of the innings. Arshdeep Singh was the pick of the attack, finishing with 3/19, while Bumrah also made an impact on his return to the T20I side. Axar Patel and Varun Chakravarthy chipped in with a wicket apiece. The disciplined bowling effort meant India needed only 157 to take the lead in the series.Abhishek Sharma turns chase into a one-sided affairIndia's chase suffered an early setback when Sanju Samson was dismissed for 10, but Afghanistan's hopes of defending the total disappeared almost immediately. Abhishek Sharma launched a spectacular counterattack, reaching his half-century in just 22 balls.The left-hander continued to take on the Afghanistan attack, eventually smashing 82 from 32 deliveries at a strike rate of 256. His seven sixes and seven fours turned what could have been a tricky chase into a procession.While Abhishek supplied the fireworks, Ishan Kishan played the ideal supporting role. Kishan scored 42 off 33 balls, helping India build a commanding partnership and maintain a huge asking-rate advantage. Abhishek eventually fell short of a century, but by then India were already within touching distance of victory.Captain Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma completed the chase, with India reaching 157/3 in only 13.4 overs.India take 1-0 leadIndia's seven-wicket victory came with 38 balls to spare, giving them a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. The second T20I will be played in Delhi on September 15, before the series concludes on September 17.Brief Scores: Afghanistan: 156/8 (Azmatullah Omarzai 64*, Mohammed Nabi 33, Arshdeep Singh 3/19) beat India: 157/3 in 13.4 overs (Abhishek Sharma 82, Ishan Kishan 42, Mohammad Nabi 2/28).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet's India avenge 2024 final defeat, beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs to lift eighth Women's Asia Cup title
articles.summary: Cricket News: India Women are back on top of Asia. Harmanpreet Kaur’s side produced a commanding all-round performance to beat Sri Lanka Women by 72 runs in the Wom.
articles.body: India Women are back on top of Asia. Harmanpreet Kaur’s side produced a commanding all-round performance to beat Sri Lanka Women by 72 runs in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2026 final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, reclaiming the continental crown and avenging their defeat in the 2024 final.After opting to bat first, India posted an imposing 183/5 in 20 overs, powered by a sensational opening partnership between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. The Indian bowlers then completed the job in emphatic fashion, bowling Sri Lanka out for 111 to seal a comprehensive victory.The victory gives India a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title and underlines their dominance in the continental tournament.Shafali, Smriti set up India’s commanding totalIndia’s innings was built around a devastating opening stand between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana.Shafali smashed 68 off just 39 balls, striking nine fours and two sixes, while Mandhana contributed a fluent 59 off 39 deliveries. Together, they added 129 runs for the opening wicket, putting Sri Lanka under immense pressure from the outset.Their aggressive batting gave India the perfect platform before Sri Lanka’s bowlers fought back with wickets in the middle overs. Gunalan Kamalini, however, provided the finishing touch with a quick-fire 15 not out from just five balls, including a huge six on the final delivery, taking India to 183/5.Sri Lanka keep themselves alive before collapseSri Lanka's chase did not begin smoothly as they lost an early wicket, but Chamari Athapaththu and Vishmi Gunaratne briefly revived their hopes with a fighting 58-run partnership. Athapaththu looked to take the attack to the Indian bowlers, while Gunaratne provided valuable support. However, with the required run rate climbing rapidly, both batters were forced to take greater risks.The breakthrough came at a crucial stage as Athapaththu was dismissed for 36 before Gunaratne followed for 20 in the same over. Their twin dismissals effectively broke Sri Lanka's resistance and swung the final decisively India's way.India’s spin attack dismantles Sri LankaOnce the partnership was broken, Sri Lanka's middle order simply could not withstand India's relentless bowling attack. The visitors slipped from 63/3 to 103/7 as wickets tumbled in quick succession. India kept attacking the stumps and denied Sri Lanka any opportunity to rebuild the innings.Shree Charani was the star with the ball, finishing with outstanding figures of 4/20 from her four overs. Her spell proved decisive as India continued to squeeze the Sri Lankan batters.Deepti Sharma also played a key role in the bowling effort, adding two crucial wickets to her already impressive tournament tally. She entered the final among the leading wicket-takers of the competition, with 11 wickets in four matches.Sri Lanka were eventually bowled out for 111 on the final ball of their innings, falling 72 runs short of India's imposing target.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India women's team refuses to take Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi after title win - WATCH
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The Indian women's cricket team refused to accept the Women's Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president and Pakistan crick.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian women's cricket team refused to accept the Women's Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president and Pakistan cricket chief Mohsin Naqvi after beating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final in Dubai on Sunday.India captain Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates were seen celebrating after their record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title. However, the Indian team did not collect the trophy from Naqvi during the presentation ceremony.The ceremony ended with Sri Lanka receiving their runners-up cheque, medals and mementoes from the officials.India refuse trophy from Mohsin NaqviNaqvi was present at the stadium as India completed a comfortable 72-run win over Sri Lanka.The cameras showed Naqvi seated alongside dignitaries, including BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla and secretary Devajit Saikia, as India sealed the title.Naqvi was later present on the stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. After Athapaththu spoke to Farvez Maharoof, the presentation ceremony came to an end.The Indian team did not collect the Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi.The incident comes a year after the controversy involving Naqvi and the Indian men's team during the Asia Cup final.During the men's Asia Cup 2025 final, chaos followed after the Indian team defeated Pakistan. The Indian players were left waiting for more than an hour to receive the trophy and medals.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Yankees secure September Subway Series as Schlittler stars, Rice and Wells go yard
articles.summary: Schlittler was close to untouchable in rubber game gem against the Mets.
articles.body:
Earlier this week , my colleague Josh asked whether Cam Schlittler could join Justin Verlander and Clayton Kershaw as the only pitchers this century to win MVP. With each successive appearance like this one, Josh's question begins to look more and more prescient. Schlittler was close to untouchable, allowing just one hit across six scoreless innings to hold serve with Dylan Cease in the AL Cy Young race. Ben Rice and Austin Wells provided all the offense with a pair of early solo home runs to right as the Yankees won the rubber game, 2-0, to secure this edition of the Subway Series (and a 3-3 split for 2026 as a whole).

Christian Scott entered this game as one of the best pitcher's in the NL when it came to his team's record in his starts, which made it important that the Yankees get on the board early. He offers a rare blend of swing and miss and damage limitation, so it was encouraging to see Rice really get into a 1-2 splitter, lining it just over the wall in right for a classic Yankee Stadium porch job.

As if you needed anything more to play for in the midst of a tense divisional race, Schlittler seemed to be pitching with an added edge this afternoon. He is neck-and-neck with Cease in the AL Cy Young race — also starting today against the Orioles — and likely wanted to answer the humiliation the Yankees faced in their drubbing the afternoon prior. He struck out four in the first two innings, three of those coming against a four-seamer that the whole Mets lineup looked nowhere close to catching up to.

Volpe got his first real test in these four games at second base and answered it with aplomb. He ranged well to his right on a sharp Brett Baty grounder, gloving it and making a jump throw to first , this shorter throwing distance seeming to suit Volpe's arm better than having to make a similar throw from in the hole at short. In the bottom of the frame, it was his chicken parm brother's turn to make his mark on this game.

Austin Wells has looked miles more competitive at the plate over the last few months after a truly abysmal start to his season. He's not giving so many pitches away and he's not missing as much when he gets what he is looking for. That being said, he entered today's contest amid an 0-for-20 skid — snapped in loud fashion in his first AB of the game. He ambushed an elevated first-pitch heater at 96 mph, launching it into the second deck in right for his eleventh home run of the year to double the Yankees' lead, 2-0.

With the way Schlittler was dealing, those two runs must have looked like a mountain to climb to the opposition. The Mets didn't manage their first hit off him until two outs into the fifth, Baty pulling a 3-1 cutter into the corner in right for a double before a Nick Morabito grounder stranded him at second.

Other than the pair of solo homers, the Yankees offer much resistance against Scott. José Caballero and Rice drew a pair of walks after the Wells homer but that came to nothing. Otherwise it was pretty smooth sailing for the Mets' second-year starter, who ended with seven strikeouts across his six innings of work including striking out the side in the fifth.

After the contact started to tick up against Schlittler in the fourth and fifth, he answered Scott's striking out of the side by ringing up Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto to open the sixth (aided by a generous check swing strike three call on Soto by the third base umpire). There was then a scary moment as Schlittler took a 112 mph liner from Bo Bichette off the back of his right thigh, the batted ball missing his pitching hand by inches. He was able to walk off the field under his own power, but went straight down the tunnel to end his outing at 94 pitches with Brent Headrick coming out to open the seventh.

If Schlittler can keep stacking starts like this, his Cy Young hopes and his team's playoff outlook will keep on improving. It's his sixth straight outing allowing one or fewer runs, extending his single-season Yankees franchise record to 21 such starts. He had to lean on four-seamer and sinker today, the curveball showing little feel while he wasn't quite able to finish his cutters, leaving a lot out of the zone to the arm-side. This elevated his pitch count to 94, which in addition to the come-backer were likely the reasons Schlittler couldn't go really deep in this start given his stuff showed no signs of degrading in his final inning. Schlittler ends the day having given up a hit and two walks with eight strikeouts in six scoreless innings to lower his season ERA below two for the first time since the first week of July.

As they've done almost without fail since the start of summer, Headrick, Paul Blackburn , and David Bednar slammed the door after Schlittler's day ended. They allowed just two hits and no walks in the final three scoreless innings, the three-headed monster nailing down another victory, 2-0, to secure the series over the crosstown rivals.

The Yankees next fly to Minnesota for three games against the Twins. Will Warren is slated to start the opener, facing off against a familiar face from his days with the Orioles in Dean Kremer . First pitch is scheduled for 7:40 pm ET on Monday with the broadcast remaining on YES.

articles.title: Big record! Abhishek Sharma achieves what 112 batters couldn't against Rashid Khan
articles.summary: Cricket News: Abhishek Sharma produced a stunning batting performance against Afghanistan in the first T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday. His 82 o.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma produced a stunning batting performance against Afghanistan in the first T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday. His 82 off 32 balls helped India chase down 157 in just 13.4 overs and take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.But Abhishek's assault also produced a remarkable record against Rashid Khan.A total of 113 batters have faced at least 30 balls from Rashid in T20 cricket in matches where ball-by-ball data is available. Abhishek's strike rate of 234.88 against Rashid, with 101 runs from 43 balls, is the highest among all 113 batters.Abhishek, Ishan dominate AfghanistanAbhishek smashed seven fours and seven sixes during his 32-ball 82. He attacked the Afghanistan bowlers from the start and put India firmly in control of the chase.He found an excellent partner in Ishan Kishan, who scored 42 off 33 balls. The pair added 121 runs for the second wicket after Sanju Samson was dismissed for 10.Abhishek and Ishan also put together the highest-ever 100-plus partnership against Afghanistan in T20Is in terms of scoring rate.Their 121 runs came from just 53 balls at a rate of 13.70 runs per over. The previous best was a scoring rate of 12.25 runs per over, when Rohit Sharma and Rinku Singh scored 190* off 93 balls in Bengaluru in 2024.India chase down 157 with easeIndia reached 82/1 in the powerplay, with Abhishek and Ishan taking the attack to the Afghanistan bowlers.Ishan and Abhishek were dismissed later in the innings, but their explosive partnership had already put India in a dominant position.Shreyas Iyer remained unbeaten on 8, while Tilak Varma finished unbeaten on 3 as India completed the chase in 13.4 overs.India take 1-0 leadIndia won the match by seven wickets to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.The two teams will meet again on Tuesday at the same venue, with Afghanistan looking to level the series and India aiming to take an unassailable lead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'One or two bad series won't define our batting': Abhishek Sharma sends clear message after India's win over Afghanistan
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Player of the Match Abhishek Sharma said on Sunday that one or two poor series cannot define the Indian cricket team. Abhishek smashed 82 i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Player of the Match Abhishek Sharma said on Sunday that one or two poor series cannot define the Indian cricket team. Abhishek smashed 82 in the first T20I against Afghanistan and made India's 157-run chase look easy at the Ferozeshah Kotla. India won by seven wickets to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.The left-handed batter said India have a clear approach of playing aggressively and looking to dominate the opposition, even if it does not always work.'One or two (bad) series won't define our batting'India had a disappointing run in their recent white-ball series against Ireland and England. They lost the T20I series in Ireland 0-2 before going down in both the T20I and ODI series in England.Abhishek, however, said the team would continue to trust its approach."I still remember two years back, we decided we want to play a certain way and dominate all teams. It worked for a year. But one or two (bad) series won't define our batting. As openers, you want to give a good start as an opener," said Sharma.Iyer credits Bumrah for setting the toneIndia captain Shreyas Iyer described the win as a collective effort and praised Jasprit Bumrah for providing the early momentum.Bumrah struck in the first over by dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz for a duck. Arshdeep Singh and the spinners then kept the pressure on as India restricted Afghanistan to 156/8."Everyone worked in synergy. Bumrah is a great asset, he created momentum for all. Arshdeep (Singh) too. Varun (Chakravarthy) continued that with Axar (Patel)."The shots Abhishek played were flawless, exemplary. (Ishan) Kishan has been in great form. He's very relaxed, calm and knows his game," said Iyer of the wicketkeeper-batter, who scored 42 off 33 balls.Afghanistan blame low totalAfghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran said his team failed to score enough runs.Afghanistan were in trouble early before making a recovery, but their total of 156/8 was not enough against India's batting."We batted well in the middle overs but didn't put up a good score. Their (Indian) bowlers and fielders did well, that run out by Kishan (of me) was the turning point I think. They're the best fielding side. Rahmanullah Gurbaz (out for zero) didn't have his day, but he will come back stronger," he hoped.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘We can’t receive the trophy from him’: Why India snubbed Mohsin Naqvi again at Women’s Asia Cup, Devajit Saikia explains
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team’s decision not to receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi was a .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team’s decision not to receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi was a show of solidarity with the men’s team, which took the same position after winning the Asia Cup last year, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...” Saikia told IANS hours after India beat Sri Lanka in Sunday's final.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia said.The decision brought back memories of the controversial presentation after the men's Asia Cup final in 2025. India had beaten Pakistan in the final, but the players were left waiting for more than an hour to receive the trophy and medals.This time, India had completed a comfortable 72-run victory over Sri Lanka to win a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title. Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates celebrated on the field, but the Indian side did not collect the trophy from Naqvi during the presentation.Naqvi was present at the stadium as India sealed the title and was seated alongside dignitaries including BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla and Saikia. He later went on stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. The presentation then ended without India receiving the trophy from him.Saikia said the decision did not take away from the team's performance.“It doesn’t diminish the performances of our team. We have won all our matches in a one-sided manner. Women’s cricket has been growing so well in India and there’s no bigger evidence of that than this. Our whole planning is geared towards the 2026 ICC T20 World Cup. The happiest part of this tournament is how India has left everyone else behind and surged so far ahead.”The presence of Naqvi alongside Saikia and Shukla in the Royal Box during the match also led to questions about the interaction between the officials.“It’s not as if we wouldn’t meet anyone. I was sitting outside in the Royal Box seats right from the toss until the end of the game. Having sat there, I remained in that same place throughout the match. Everyone who came met me during the match; someone sat next to me, then Shukla came and sat with me. The person you mentioned also came and sat alongside Deputy Chairman Khalid (Khalid Al Zarooni) sahib. That’s just a normal tradition—whenever anyone comes, we meet and talk with everyone,” Saikia said.Saikia said there had been an attempt to resolve the trophy presentation issue.“We tried to solve today's situation, but our efforts were not successful. We don’t have any regrets. Our ultimate priority and ambition was not to focus on who would give the trophy. We wanted the Indian team to win and we’ve achieved that.”He also said his interaction with Naqvi was not centred on the trophy. Saikia had presented the fielding medal after the game and said the conversation around that was about India's next assignment.“I also got the chance to give the fielding medal that’s given out after every game. The conversation that was had around that was about the Asian Games, not about whether the trophy should be taken or not.”India's attention now shifts to the Asian Games in Japan's Aichi Prefecture. The team is scheduled to play on September 18, 20 and 22.“Currently, there are no such plans. Right now, our focus is on tomorrow, as our team will be leaving for Japan via Delhi. So, all our attention is set on the Asian Games starting in Japan, where our matches are scheduled for the 18th, 20th and 22nd. Our goal is to bring home the gold medal, and that is our sole objective.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘We are the champions’: Amol Muzumdar backs BCCI stand as India skip Women’s Asia Cup trophy presentation with Mohsin Naqvi
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India women’s head coach Amol Muzumdar has backed the Board of Control for Cricket in India’s (BCCI) decision to not accept the Women’s Asi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India women’s head coach Amol Muzumdar has backed the Board of Control for Cricket in India’s (BCCI) decision to not accept the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi, saying the team stood united behind the board’s position after their emphatic 72-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final.The presentation ceremony at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday became the latest flashpoint involving Naqvi, who is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and Pakistan’s Interior Minister. As Sri Lanka collected their runners-up medals and skipper Chamari Athapaththu received the runners-up cheque from Naqvi, the Indian players were conspicuous by their absence.Muzumdar, however, insisted that India’s focus was firmly on the achievement rather than the trophy presentation.“The stand has been taken by the BCCI. We stand by it. For us, this tournament is over. We are the champions. That's good enough. This tournament is over. Officially over for us,” Muzumdar told reporters after the final.“It was on the big board that India, the champions of Asia Cup 2026. We are happy that we've turned out to be champions. Now, we look forward to the Asian Games,” he added.India stay away from trophy presentationThe decision had been anticipated because of the precedent set during last year’s men’s Asia Cup. India’s men had also refused to collect the trophy from Naqvi after defeating Pakistan in the final amid heightened tensions between the two countries following the Pahalgam terror attack and subsequent border hostilities.On Sunday, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were seen speaking to the Indian players after the victory. Before the official ceremony, the team also held its own celebrations, with Saikia and Shukla congratulating the players and presenting pacer Nandani Sharma with the ‘Fielder of the Match’ medal.When the official presentation began, however, the Indian players did not come onto the field. Sri Lanka’s players received their runners-up medals from the dignitaries before the ceremony ended without India collecting the championship trophy from Naqvi.When asked whether there was any update on the trophy and whether India would eventually receive it, Muzumdar was unequivocal.“No news. I cannot answer about this,” he said.‘We’re united and standing by it’Pressed further on the decision, Muzumdar reiterated that it was the BCCI’s position and that the Indian side had collectively chosen to stand behind it.“The stand has been taken by the BCCI, and we're united and standing by it. For us, this tournament is officially over. The fact that we're champions, we're really glad, and I'm really proud of every single person in this unit, including the support staff and the players, needless to say. We're looking forward to the Asian Games now,” he said.The controversy did little to overshadow India’s commanding performance in the final.India dominate Sri Lanka to win eighth titleAfter being asked to bat first, India posted a formidable 183/5, with openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma producing a record-breaking start. Mandhana struck 59 off 39 balls, while Shafali smashed 68 off 39, including nine fours and two sixes, as the pair added 129 for the first wicket.India’s bowlers then completed the job, dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 20 overs. Sree Charani claimed 4/20, while Deepti Sharma returned 3/19 as India sealed a comprehensive 72-run victory.Muzumdar praised the entire squad after India secured their eighth Asia Cup title.“Fantastic effort. They showed up from the first game and, fittingly, finished it off strong. Really proud of all the players and all the support staff as well,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on the bench: Why India's bold T20I vision feels incomplete
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer called having to pick between Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryanshi and Abhishek Sharma as a \"luxury to have for.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer called having to pick between Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryanshi and Abhishek Sharma as a "luxury to have for any side." More often than not, the challenge is to pick between Samson and Sooryavanshi. One brings experience, and the other brings a no-holds-barred approach.That was the case as the T20I series between India and Afghanistan got underway on Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. No clear signs of one or the other emerged as the teams went through the motions. Abhishek did some shadow batting. Sooryavanshi lined up to take some aerial catches. India coach Gautam Gambhir pinged Samson's wicketkeeping gloves.As the team went into a huddle and emerged, both Samson and Sooryavanshi found their way onto the dugout. Both kept their poker faces well. Ishan Kishan, one of the wicketkeeping options in the squad, spoke for a considerable period with batting coach Sitanshu Kotak.The mystery box was opened at the toss when Shreyas Iyer announced that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Washington Sundar and two more (Ravi Bishnoi and Yash Thakur) were not in the playing XI. His reasoning to Sanjay Manjrekar was near incoherent."That is more difficult, I feel, but I would say if Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, then Washington (Sundar) is not playing and there are two more which you'll get to know," he said on managing team combinations and selecting players for the match.When it came to it, Sanju Samson scored just 10 runs from 8 balls with two boundaries to show for it. His brief stay in the middle was halted by Azmatullah Omarzai, giving catching practice to Darwish Rasooli at deep square leg in the process. On a surface that needed patience before getting going, as Abhishek Sharma demonstrated with a 32-ball 82, the 31-year-old had not made the most of the opportunity.The question of batting order that Iyer didn't answer with conviction at the toss was probed again with Abhishek Sharma and Varun Chakaravarthy after India's 7-wicket win with 38 balls to spare."I still remember two years back, we decided we want to play a certain way and dominate all teams. It worked for a year. But one or two (bad) series won't define our batting. As openers, you want to give a good start as an opener," said Sharma, whose 82-run knock earned him the Player of the Match.Varun, meanwhile, praised India's top order for how lethal they are against spinners."Against our team, batting line-up, you can't bowl spin. So, if you bowl spin against our batting line-up, they are just going to smack (you) left, right and centre. We are so used to playing spinners. We have one of the best batting line-ups and our top-8 can take on any spinner in the world. I have personally bowled against them, played against them. I know how hard it is. So, yeah, I feel for the spinners," said the spinner who had an economical return from injury.The question, however, persists over Sooryavanshi's place in the team and the long-term approach in the format. Samson's presence adds a wicketkeeping option and a left-right pairing at the top of the order. But, with all due respect to Samson's abilities, it steals what can be a game-changing and game-deciding pairing of Abhishek-Sooryavanshi.Samson posted single-digit scores against Ireland and in the first T20I against England before allowing Sooryavanshi to come in and make his India debut. Sooryavanshi couldn't do much either, with 42 runs from three matches.But as Samson was rested for the tour to Zimbabwe and Sooryavanshi became the de facto choice, the 15-year-old produced a series-topping 151 runs from three matches at a strike rate of 196.10.With India set to play two T20Is against Afghanistan, a one-off T20I against Japan, the Asian Games, five T20Is against West Indies, five T20Is against New Zealand and three T20Is against Sri Lanka in 2026, the can of worms involving Sooryavanshi has been opened with his absence.The sole reason Sooryavanshi was included in squads for Ireland and England, and fast-tracked into the Indian team at all of 15, was to give wings to this sensational talent. Not playing him, in favour of Samson's experience, does grave disservice to him, his talent and Indian cricket at large.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Proud moment for Indian cricket’: PM Modi, President Murmu hail India after historic Women’s Asia Cup triumph
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu led the tributes on Monday as India celebrated the women’s eighth Women’s Asia Cu.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu led the tributes on Monday as India celebrated the women’s eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, with both praising Harmanpreet Kaur’s side for an unbeaten and dominant campaign.India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday to extend their record in the continental tournament. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma powered India to 183/5 before Sree Charani and Deepti Sharma spearheaded a disciplined bowling effort that restricted Sri Lanka to 111.The triumph prompted congratulatory messages from across the country, with Modi highlighting the confidence and consistency shown by the side throughout the tournament.‘A proud moment for Indian cricket’: PM Modi congratulates Team India“A proud moment for Indian cricket! Congratulations to the Women’s team on winning the Asia Cup. Their confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit were on full display throughout the tournament. May this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine,” PM Modi wrote on X.President Droupadi Murmu also congratulated the players, describing the achievement as a source of inspiration, particularly for young women.“My heartiest congratulations to all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. They played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches. They have done the country proud. They are a source of great inspiration for our youth, especially our daughters. I am sure, they will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence,” the President’s official handle posted on X.Shukla, Dhami and Puri hail dominant campaignBCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla also praised the team for maintaining an unbeaten record and credited every member for contributing to the title.“What a performance by our Women in Blue! Undefeated throughout the tournament and now Asia Cup champions for the 8th time Every player stepped up when required. A complete team effort and a proud moment for Indian cricket. Well played, Team India!” Shukla wrote on X.Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami praised the side’s discipline and confidence, calling the achievement a matter of pride for the country.Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri also lauded India’s all-round display.“What a day it was for Indian sports! Another big win for India! A dominating show by Team India to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs to lift the Women’s Asia Cup Cricket 2026 in Dubai for a record eight time! Batting brilliance. Bowling firepower. Electric fielding. Nerves of steel. Every department fired. Every moment belonged to India. Take a bow, Champions! You’ve made the tricolour fly higher and a billion cheers roar louder!” Puri wrote on X.India’s victory was built around a record 129-run opening partnership between Mandhana and Shafali. Mandhana scored 59 off 39 balls, while Shafali made 68 off 39. Sree Charani then claimed 4/20 and Deepti Sharma returned 3/19 as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111.Saikia explains India’s decision over trophy presentationThe celebrations were accompanied by a politically sensitive moment during the trophy presentation, as India did not receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the decision was a show of solidarity with the men’s side, which had taken a similar position after winning the 2025 Asia Cup.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...” Saikia told IANS.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” he said.Saikia stressed that the decision did not diminish the achievement.“It doesn’t diminish the performances of our team. We have won all our matches in a one-sided manner. Women’s cricket has been growing so well in India and there’s no bigger evidence of that than this. Our whole planning is geared towards the 2026 ICC T20 World Cup. The happiest part of this tournament is how India has left everyone else behind and surged so far ahead.”India’s focus now shifts to the Asian Games in Japan’s Aichi Prefecture, with Saikia saying the team’s immediate objective is clear.“Currently, there are no such plans. Right now, our focus is on tomorrow, as our team will be leaving for Japan via Delhi. So, all our attention is set on the Asian Games starting in Japan, where our matches are scheduled for the 18th, 20th and 22nd. Our goal is to bring home the gold medal, and that is our sole objective.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India thrive in home comfort: Bumrah hits stride on comeback as Iyer’s men crush Afghanistan in first T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah’s first delivery of the night drifted past Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s pads and beat wicketkeeper Sanju Samson to the boundary for .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah’s first delivery of the night drifted past Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s pads and beat wicketkeeper Sanju Samson to the boundary for five wides. That was the only time one could say he was coming off an injury layoff. Two deliveries later, he got the ball to kick from a good length for Gurbaz to awkwardly fend it to first slip. From there, usual business resumed for India’s T20I team on home soil after a winless tour of Ireland and England two months ago.The Indian bowling attack, led by Bumrah, stifled Afghanistan to 156/8.Opener Abhishek Sharma effortlessly blazed away to 82 off 32 and Ishan Kishan eased to 42 off 33 as India cantered to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series with seven wickets and 38 balls to spare with captain Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma completing the formalities at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday evening.On paper, Afghanistan are the hosts of this T20I series. But the Indian T20I team re-established this as their hunting ground. As is often the case with Bumrah, that one menacing delivery to Gurbaz shook the confidence of the Afghanistan batting. And as usual, Bumrah set the tone for the rest of the attack to settle down on a length against an unsure batting lineup.Call it the impact of Bumrah’s spell of 1/26 or playing in Indian conditions, India’s new T20I captain Iyer finally got to see how ominous this team can be after taking over the reins from Suryakumar Yadav post the T20 World Cup triumph at home.Azmatullah Omarzai’s enterprising unbeaten 64 off 44 balls dragged Afghanistan out of the ditch at 43/5 to post 156/8. Bumrah’s arrival just goes to show the difference he makes to an attack.Going by their records, Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel and Varun Chakravarthy were expected to have the upper hand against a comparatively inexperienced Afghan batting lineup. That said, this same attack without Bumrah came second in all six T20Is on the tour of Ireland and England. The incisive opening burst allowed Arshdeep, Axar and Varun to apply the choke as they returned figures of 3/19, 1/27 and 1/16.Bumrah has predominantly played T20 cricket over last year. Most of it has been on scary flat decks. Sunday’s pitch at the Ferozeshah Kotla was a tired one after enduring the load of the IPL and Delhi Premier League T20.Help of any kind from the surface is enough for Bumrah to get into the minds of the batters. From letting it rip with the new ball to using the dual nature of the pitch with his cutters, he flaunted his wares in his first T20 game after the IPL. If one crack in India’s T20 cricket stood exposed on Sunday night, it was the lack of decent bowling allrounder. Even as Omarzai went about rebuilding the innings with veteran Mohammed Nabi, the run rate dipped below six runs per over by the 10th over with India’s frontline bowlers operating with immaculate accuracy. The shackles were broken only when seamers Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube were taken for 0/30 in two overs and 21 off one over respectively.Brief scores: Afghanistan 156-8 in 20 overs (Azmatullah Omarzai 64 not out, Mohammad Nabi 33; Arshdeep Singh 3-19, Varun Chakravarthy 1-16) lost to India 157-3 in 13.4 overs (Abhishek Sharma 82, Ishan Kishan 42; Mohammad Nabi 2-28) by seven wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Women’s Asia Cup: Shafali, Smriti’s stunning opening act powers India to eighth title
articles.summary: Cricket News: At last, India got a batting beauty and made the most of it, thanks to their in-form openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. Continuing her blazing.
articles.body: At last, India got a batting beauty and made the most of it, thanks to their in-form openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. Continuing her blazing form, Shafali smashed 68 off 39, adding 129 in just 77 balls with fellow superstar and vice-captain Mandhana (59 off 39), who also stroked a half-century, as India defeated defending champions Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup final to clinch a record eighth title at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Shree Charani snapped four wickets to hasten Sri Lanka’s downfall.In a murderous mood, Shafali took just 24 balls to reach her 21st fifty, erasing Mandhana’s 25-ball effort in 2022 as the fastest fifty in Women’s Asia Cup history. Mandhana reached her 36th T20I half century in 35 balls. Given the start they got, India would be disappointed at not reaching 200 after a middle-order muddle. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur (14, 14b, 1x4), Richa Ghosh (17, 13b, 1x4, 1x6) and Deepti Sharma (5, 7b) fell cheaply as Sri Lanka staged a fine fightback.India recovered towards the end through a fine cameo from G Kamalini (15*, 5b, 1x4, 1x6), who was surprisingly included in the XI after India dropped out-of-form No. 3 Pratika Rawal. Kamalini skipped down the track to edge Sugandika Kumari for four before finishing the innings in style by dancing down the track and depositing the bowler over cow corner. Sri Lanka also suffered a major blow when batter Vishmi Gunarathne was stretchered off after twisting her ankle while fielding. The injury leaves the pressure of a stiff 184-run chase on captain Chamari Athapaththu and her team.Shafali, who cracked her third half century of the tournament — all three scores have been in the 60s — and Mandhana took the Sri Lankan attack to the cleaners on perhaps the best batting surface of the tournament. With 236 runs in five matches at 47.20 and a strike rate of 171.01, Shafali is set to finish as the tournament’s leading run-scorer. Mandhana, with 213 runs at 42.60 and a strike rate of 165.11, is set to finish second.Shafali targeted Athapaththu in the latter’s first over, creaming her for 6, 6 and 4 as the Sri Lankan skipper conceded 20 runs. India raced to 57 in the Powerplay and reached 98 at the halfway mark without losing a wicket. Much to Sri Lanka’s relief, the stand ended when Shafali slapped Praboda straight to Athapaththu at the edge of the circle.Mandhana, though, would be disappointed to have been run out for the third time in this Asia Cup. In a debatable decision, she sacrificed her wicket in the 14th over after Harmanpreet cut a ball to point and set off, leaving her partner with little option but to go through with the run. It was a poor call by Harmanpreet, though Mandhana could have turned it down.Brief scores: India Women 183/5 in 20 overs (S Verma 68, S Mandhana 59; C Praboda 1/40) beat Sri Lanka Women 111 all out in 20 overs (C Athapaththu 36, N Silva 22; S Charani 4-20, D Sharma 3-19) by 72 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kevin Pietersen 'buzzing' at England white-ball coaching role as specialist mentor, says Marcus Trescothick
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen "buzzing" for England role and will add "a little more spark" to white-ball sides, says batting coach Marcus Trescothick; watch the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, Tuesday (first ball 6.30pm)
articles.body:
Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm.

Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team.

"He is buzzing about putting back on the England shirt or tracksuit, buzzing for the opportunity and it's really exciting," the England batting coach said of Pietersen.

"Having his presence around, and the knowledge he has about batting - he saw batting in a different light to many people - if we can tap into that and get that into our white-ball cricket, It's only going to benefit the team."

Is Pietersen appointment a risk? | 'He'll add a little more spark', says Trescothick

The appointment has raised a few eyebrows, coming 12 years after Pietersen was effectively sacked by the ECB in the wake of England's disastrous 5-0 Ashes drubbing in Australia. At the time, the ECB said he had become "disconnected" from the team and accused him of failing to support then-captain Sir Alastair Cook.

Pietersen had previously been dropped in 2012 after sending text messages to members of the South African team, while he resigned as captain after just five months in 2008 following a breakdown in his relationship with then head coach Peter Moores.

Since his retiring a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, also been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after Brendon McCullum had just taken over as head coach, who he'll now be working under.

Having hammered India 4-0 in a T20 series earlier this summer, briefly leapfrogging them at the top of the world rankings, and won their last two ODI series against Sri Lanka and India, England's decision to hire Pietersen appears a risky move at a time when the team is enjoying a strong run of form.

"You can see the team moving in the right direction; we've had great results in the last sort of 18 months - in both formats," Trescothick said, before adding: "I think you're just adding a little more spark and a little bit more variety from a different coach's point of view.

"Kevin has seen white-ball cricket around the world for a long period of time, playing in all the big competitions, he's won a [T20] World Cup [in 2010], you're going to gain something extra.

"It's up to the coaching setup with Brendon to draw out the best from him.

"Management of different players, coaches and setups is is the great art, isn't it? If you get that right, then you get a lot of good things come from coaches and players alike."
